initial_requirements: Georgia Library PINES needs improved management and reporting capabilities within its shared integrated library system. Library managers, directors, staff, and consortium administrators should be able to analyze collection use, branch capacity, patron interests, staff workflows, and financial activity across participating libraries. The system should support both local decision-making and consortium-wide oversight without disrupting the operational services used by patrons and library staff.

topics.topic_content: Circulation and service operations supporting staff oversight

slots.key: Operational service metrics needed by staff managers
slots.value: Essential reporting inputs include circulation transactions, holds activity, item and bibliographic records, branch and location identifiers, patron category or group, and basic financial records tied to fines, fees, losses, or replacements. For some reports, staff activity and workload data are also needed when leaders are evaluating service levels or staffing pressure across branches. More specialized reports may additionally require collection counts, format or subject breakdowns, and historical snapshots, but these are not required for every report. The reporting flow also needs to pull data from the ILS and related records, generate a usable report, and make it available for staff to view, export, or share with leadership for decisions without interrupting daily patron service or requiring re-entry of data elsewhere. Operational sources like circulation, holds, and item status should refresh very frequently, ideally near real time or at least several times a day, because staff use those numbers for active decisions. Financial and historical summary data can update less often, maybe nightly, since they’re usually reviewed in batches and don’t need minute-by-minute changes. Anything used for long-term trend reporting can be refreshed on a scheduled basis as long as leaders know the data currency.

revisions.new_value: Live transaction data should update very frequently, ideally near real time or at least throughout the day, because staff need it for current activity and immediate checks; posted financial summaries can update on a nightly or end-of-day cycle; historical totals can refresh less often since they’re mainly for trend reporting; during reconciliation and month-end closing, some totals may need a different schedule or a temporary freeze so the numbers stay stable while finance staff are balancing them.

slots.value: Branch alerts should be based primarily on the branch’s own historical baseline rather than a universal threshold. Trigger when there is a sustained rise above that baseline or repeated peaks occurring at the same times over several cycles. A single busy period should not trigger an alert unless it is unusually extreme.

revisions.new_value: Consistently above threshold on seating use, meeting room use, or general space utilization should trigger a possible capacity review, staffing adjustments, or space changes; consistently below threshold should also prompt a closer look as a planning signal, not an automatic problem, since low use may still be appropriate in some communities.
